sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: Passiflora tarminiana is a climbing vine native to the Andes, cultivated and naturalised elsewhere. It is sometimes confused with Passiflora tripartita var. mollissima, but the catalogue treats them separately.

sections.title: Flowers and fruit
sections.text: The open flowers are about 8–9 cm across and the floral tube is 6–8 cm long. The pale pink segments are 2.5–4 cm long; the corona is purple with pink markings. The elongated yellow-orange fruit contains orange pulp and arils.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: The ripe fruit is described as sweet and edible. The plant can become invasive in New Zealand.
